templates_considered: AUTH-002 admin_endpoints_check_role: fits part 1 (admin endpoints call role check first). Used as base; its example tag scope ['admin'] replaced by api_groups because the workspace has no admin tag, only the 'admin' API group, and I cannot add tags.
AUTH-020 own_records_only: did not fit. Its where-constraint is on a user owner field against $auth.id; the ask is an org_id filter with no logged-in-user comparison.
AUTH-030 no_self_promotion, AUTH-003, BIZ-001, AUTH-040, AUTH-050: did not fit the ask.
DATA-010 no_pii_in_responses, CONF-010 sensitive_tables_need_login: did not fit; the ask is about a query filter, not fields or login.
AUTH-010 endpoints_need_login: did not fit; ask does not require enabling auth, and the admin endpoints already use auth='users'.

rules.covers: every endpoint under /admin must check the role before doing anything else (as the first statement)
never touches the tenants table without filtering by org_id

ask_parts_not_covered.part: endpoints under /admin: the role values 'admin' or 'support_lead' are tested in check_admin_role, not by the policy
endpoints under /admin: path prefix, since no scope field matches URL path; api/app/admin/stats_GET is served at /admin/stats in the app group and is not covered
'before doing anything else' as a strict rule: the check only verifies the call is the first statement, not that nothing else precedes it via middleware
org_id filter must match the caller's org: no check ties a filter value to the logged-in user's org; compare_to would need a reference the workspace may not have (no org on $auth known)

assumptions: 'endpoints under /admin' means the API group named admin (canonical admin), whose comment says it is served at /api:admin
check_admin_role is the role-check function the ask refers to
tenants.org_id is the field the ask means by org_id
no compare_to for org_id, because the admin staff user is not in an org; a filter on any value satisfies the ask as written
workspace_names_used: endpoints api/admin/users_GET, api/admin/tenants_GET, api/admin/tenants/tenant_id_PATCH, api/admin/orgs/org_id/tenants_GET, api/app/admin/stats_GET
table users (role field used by check_admin_role)
confusions: AUTH-002 template example uses tags ['admin'] in its rule, but the workspace's admin endpoints carry the API group, not an admin tag; the template does not say whether to swap to api_groups or add a tag, and I could not add one.

object.statement_required rule warning: api_groups only selects endpoints, so object_kinds must be set to ['query'] to say so. The catalogue lists the scope fields as endpoint-only but does not say this is required for the warning to clear.
No scope param matches URL path. The ask says 'under /admin'; the skill says to scope by tag, not name, but the workspace has no tag for admin endpoints.
Whether a db.query count (stats) counts as a read for db.where_constraint_required is not stated; I expect it does, unverified.
The skill says 'write only names the workspace has' and 'check the tables', but the template's example keys (require_admin) do not match the workspace's check_admin_role; I used the workspace name.
wished_for: A path-prefix scope (for example path_prefix: '/admin') or an endpoint scope by URL, so 'under /admin' can be stated directly.
A recipe for 'check role first' that names how to pass a user's role, not only the user id.
An example of db.where_constraint_required on a table with no owner-user relation (org scoping), since AUTH-020 only shows the user case.
Guidance on whether a count query or a read inside a called function is judged by db.where_constraint_required.
parse_errors_seen: AUTH-002.R1: api_groups only matches endpoints, so this rule inspects endpoints only; set object_kinds: ["query"] to say so. (warning, fixed)
why_confidence: Both policies parse with no warnings after the fix, and both use real workspace names. Confidence is not higher because the path-prefix scope cannot be expressed (api/app/admin/stats_GET escapes AUTH-002), and the org_id filter checks presence of a filter, not that it equals the caller's org. I did not evaluate, so the findings are predictions from reading the workspace.
